reports.title: School transportation: what the buses cost, and who pays
reports.about: What the school buses cost and who pays: the school day against athletics, budgeted and spent, every year since FY2010; athletic buses sport by sport, with our estimate of the trips the dollars buy; and what the Dee Bus contract fixes through FY2028.

reports.title: The FY26 school surplus, from the period-13 ledger
reports.about: What the period-13 ledger shows was left unspent in the school general fund in FY2026, against the range the June ledger allowed and what the Committee was told.

reports.title: The FY25 school surplus, from the closed ledger
reports.about: What the closed ledger shows was left unspent in the school general fund when FY2025 ended, beside the figure the School Committee was told.

reports.title: The annual town reports
reports.about: The sixteen annual town reports, FY2011–FY2025, every one downloadable with the sha256 of the bytes we hold — and what we read out of them, by category. Says plainly which pages tie to a total the page itself prints and which carry figures nothing has ever checked, because those are not the same thing.

reports.title: Open seats
reports.about: Which of the town’s boards and committees has a seat going spare, and when the filled ones come up. A list rather than a report: the one page here somebody reads and then does something about. Regenerated by the daily refresh.

reports.title: Board composition
reports.about: How the town’s boards are made up — which are biggest, how fast each turns over, and whether the establishment is growing. The seats barely move; about a third of the people in them change every year.

reports.title: Who works for the town
reports.about: How many people each part of the town employs, department by department, from the counts the town states in its own annual reports — a named roster, an establishment of posts, or a figure spelled out in prose. A minority of departments publish one and the rest publish nothing, and the page says which is which and why. The seats people volunteer for are on the board-composition report.

reports.title: The stabilization option
reports.about: What the stabilization funds could actually do about the school budget gap. Spending the whole spendable balance buys two years; stopping the deposits is permanent and covers a quarter of the first year. Neither closes it, and they fail differently.

reports.title: Solid Waste & Recycling: what the town votes for it
reports.about: Trash and recycling — the fastest-growing line in the budget by rate, and small enough that the rate moves the total very little. Every budget line the town prints beneath it, FY2023 to FY2025, reconciled against the department total on the same page.

reports.title: Schools: what the town votes for it
reports.about: The largest line in the town budget by a long way, and not the fastest growing one. Lunenburg Public Schools and the Monty Tech assessment. Every budget line the town prints beneath it, FY2023 to FY2025, reconciled against the department total on the same page.

reports.title: Public Works: what the town votes for it
reports.about: Highway, vehicle maintenance for three departments, the Park and Cemetery departments, and snow removal. Every budget line the town prints beneath it, FY2023 to FY2025, reconciled against the department total on the same page.

reports.title: Protection of persons & property: what the town votes for it
reports.about: Police, Fire, Radio Watch and the inspectors, each with its own printed subtotal beneath the department total. Every budget line the town prints beneath it, FY2023 to FY2025, reconciled against the department total on the same page.

reports.title: Maturing Debt & Interest: what the town votes for it
reports.about: The town’s debt service — the only line in the voted budget that falls, and it falls by a third in three years. Where that room went is the cross-department report’s question, not this page’s. Every budget line the town prints beneath it, FY2023 to FY2025, reconciled against the department total on the same page.

reports.title: Library: what the town votes for it
reports.about: One line, one library. Every budget line the town prints beneath it, FY2023 to FY2025, reconciled against the department total on the same page.

reports.title: Health & Sanitation: what the town votes for it
reports.about: Board of Health, the Nashoba association, nursing and mental health — under a fifth of a percent of the budget. Every budget line the town prints beneath it, FY2023 to FY2025, reconciled against the department total on the same page.

reports.title: General Government: what the town votes for it
reports.about: The town’s own administration — the Select Board, the Town Manager, the Accountant, the Clerk, the Assessors, IT and legal. Every budget line the town prints beneath it, FY2023 to FY2025, reconciled against the department total on the same page.

reports.title: Facilities & Grounds: what the town votes for it
reports.about: The buildings the town owns and the grounds around them. Every budget line the town prints beneath it, FY2023 to FY2025, reconciled against the department total on the same page.

reports.title: Employee benefits & reserves: what the town votes for it
reports.about: Printed `Gen Gov Unclassified`, and seven tenths of it is group health insurance. The fastest-growing large line in the budget, and the one that moves the total more than the schools do. Every budget line the town prints beneath it, FY2023 to FY2025, reconciled against the department total on the same page.

reports.title: Central Purchasing: what the town votes for it
reports.about: The smallest line in the budget and the flattest. It is here because a department that does not move is a finding about the ones that do. Every budget line the town prints beneath it, FY2023 to FY2025, reconciled against the department total on the same page.

reports.title: Budgets across town
reports.about: What Town Meeting voted for each of the twelve town departments, and which of them actually move the total. It refuses the question it is most often asked — an omnibus budget cannot show a deficit, because a town may not vote one — and answers the useful version: ten of twelve departments grew faster than the levy cap, and the biggest line is not the fastest.

reports.title: Assistance: what the town votes for it
reports.about: The Council on Aging and Veterans’ services, each with its own printed subtotal. Every budget line the town prints beneath it, FY2023 to FY2025, reconciled against the department total on the same page.

reports.title: The stabilization funds, and who may spend them
reports.about: The town’s savings, fund by fund: what each one holds, who may spend it, what it may be spent ON, and the meeting that created it. Whether any of it can cover a school deficit is a question of purpose and of vote, not of balance.

reports.title: How Lunenburg compares, and what matching would cost
reports.about: Lunenburg beside the districts people name at meetings — including the regional ones, because "regionalize and we get more money" is a top-five talking point about this deficit. Per-pupil spending, what the state pays, what the district itself funds, and what the tax bill is in each town.

reports.title: Hiring here instead of placing there
reports.about: The district’s own argument — that hiring special education staff in district avoids out-of-district placements — and why this archive cannot yet test it. A scoping note, not a finding: what it would take to answer is the whole point of it.

reports.about: Youth sports and the town: the funds that field and facility money runs through, what goes in and out of them, which leagues use the fields, and what the boards have said about the arrangement since 2014.

reports.title: The boards, compared
reports.about: How the boards post: for every board the town posts for, the share of its meetings that got minutes, by fiscal year, and how many were recorded.

reports.about: The School Committee’s finances, every line: the appropriation, its revolving funds, grants, gifts and trusts, with what each held at 31 March 2026 and what it has done since FY2011 — the first of a page per board and department, from a registry of every accounting measure the town prints.

reports.title: Teacher contracts
reports.about: What the next teachers’ settlement is worth to the gap per half a point, what holding the line to the cap means in positions, and what smaller raises would have changed.

reports.title: School user and athletic fees
reports.about: What athletic, activity and bus fees can add at the most each can ever raise — every fee has a peak — and how many years that covers.

reports.title: Parks & Recreation — the department, its fund, its sales, its grounds
reports.about: Parks & Recreation: what the department is voted, what its own fee fund holds and has done since FY2011, what the registration system took in for FY2025, and what a contractor bid to keep the grounds.

reports.title: Health insurance
reports.about: What Massachusetts law lets a town do about health insurance, what each option costs somebody, and what every municipality in the Commonwealth has spent since FY2002.

reports.title: Free cash — can it fill the gap?
reports.about: Whether free cash can fill the gap: yes, once, inside the town’s own guideline — for one year, out of the capital plan’s money, and budgeting tighter moves the same dollars a year earlier.

reports.title: Extracurriculars — sports, music and clubs
reports.about: Every sport, the band, the clubs and the art supplies still funded, eliminated: what it saves, and that it buys one year.

reports.title: Classroom positions and class size
reports.about: The gap in classroom positions at the district’s own cost per post, what is already cut, and why this is the line every other option exists to avoid.

reports.title: Homes and students — the town builds, the schools do not grow
reports.about: Homes and students: the town’s single-family parcel count and the schools’ headcount, FY1994 to FY2026, side by side — the town has added homes every year and the schools have not gained children.

reports.title: Commercial development and new growth
reports.about: The commercial base as the state certifies it, FY2002 to FY2026: how big it is, what share of the town it is, and how much of it was built rather than revalued.

reports.title: The budget feed — every board, everything about money
reports.about: What every board is doing to prepare for Town Meeting: the omnibus budget, the school budget above all, and the warrant. What is coming, where this cycle stands, what was said most recently, what was posted. Not every mention of money — the budget being built, and what will land on the warrant.

reports.title: The boards — each one, in one place
reports.about: Every board and committee the town posts for, one page each: what is coming, what happened, every vote we have minutes for, where the board’s time goes, and when budget season has fallen on its agendas in past years.

reports.title: Lunenburg’s homes and the tax bill
reports.about: Lunenburg’s homes and the tax bill: how many there are, what the average one is worth and pays, year by year and against the neighbours — and, behind that, how long the owners have been here and what a long-held home pays.
